subject.title: fix: active-memory recall fails with billing rejections on subscription-only Claude CLI setups

question: Should this fix establish `cliBackendDispatch` plus a public eligibility resolver as the permanent plugin/runtime contract, or should Claude subscription routing be expressed through provider-owned CLI backend capability metadata?
rationale: Both shapes can fix the reproduced bug, but repository policy assigns provider-specific auth and routing behavior to the provider owner while public plugin runtime additions become long-lived compatibility commitments.

options.title: Use provider capability metadata
options.body: Move Claude subscription eligibility behind `CliBackendConfig` and let the generic embedded runner and active-memory consume the resulting execution plan.

options.title: Approve the current API
options.body: Accept the new run parameter and plugin runtime resolver as supported contracts, with focused compatibility documentation and API-key upgrade proof.

options.title: Narrow the integration
options.body: Keep the dispatch and eligibility helpers internal to active-memory and embedded-run implementation until a broader plugin API use case is established.

recommendation.title: Use provider capability metadata
recommendation.body: Move Claude subscription eligibility behind `CliBackendConfig` and let the generic embedded runner and active-memory consume the resulting execution plan.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person most directly to Claude CLI runtime behavior and the CLI tool-permission boundary affected by the API decision.
